candidates.name: Theorem 6.1`s own hypotheses, against the Epstein form
candidates.why: Theorem 6.1 ranges over cuspidal automorphic representations, whose L-functions each carry an Euler product; the record measured that the Epstein function has none. The second object is outside the class by hypothesis.
quotes: there is no Euler product to keep it

candidates.name: Theorem 6.1 over the two-element class {zeta, Z_Q} by the finite maximum
candidates.why: Over a finite class the maximum of the constants IS one constant, so the interchange is free (BAR 7) -- but the maximum needs a constant for each member, and Theorem 6.1 supplies none for Z_Q. The failure is membership, not uniformity.
quotes: the corpus’s second object is **not established to be one**

quotes: Dedekind zeta functions of any algebraic

candidates.name: CC`s statements

candidates.name: row F7`s own measured statements
candidates.why: The row speaks of both objects, so S1 passes; but what it holds is measured at finitely many cells, and a measurement is not a constant serving every representation.
quotes: the formula closes for the Epstein function at 21 of 21 cells below its ceiling

candidates.name: b325`s transfer of the archimedean distribution
candidates.why: A constant shared across the two objects would need the archimedean side to transfer between them; the record measured that it does not.
quotes: THE ARCHIMEDEAN DISTRIBUTION DOES NOT TRANSFER

candidates.why: THE NEAR-MISS OF THE SITE: the constant IS uniform across representations, carried by the conductor -- but only across cuspidal ones, it bounds the counting function and not the finite-place sum, and Lagarias cites it from a source the record does not hold. candidates.name: Theorem 3.1 on the Li class L of test functions
candidates.why: The test-function class L does not depend on the object, which is why it was hand-picked; the theorem that uses it still quantifies over cuspidal pi.
